<USER_SCRIPT>
CORAL — A SUMMER LAUNCH

Bondi Studio - Morning in front of her microphone

Sunlight floods a white vanity. SCARLETT (19, blonde, sun-kissed),
a Bondi influencer, unboxes a coral lipstick and turns it slowly
to camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
One shade. One summer.

CLOSE ON THE TUBE — the coral bullet twists up and catches the
light. Scarlett smiles at her reflection, the colour already hers.

EXT. BONDI BEACH PROMENADE - CONTINUOUS

Scarlett walks the promenade, blonde hair lifting in the breeze,
surfers cresting behind her. She glances back at camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
Made for the water. Wear it everywhere.

EXT. BONDI BEACH - SHORELINE - CONTINUOUS

She laughs as a wave breaks at her feet. The lipstick lands
beside the brand mark in the sand.

SUPER:  CORAL.  OUT NOW.
</USER_SCRIPT>

Target video duration: 1 minute (about 8-12 scenes). Give each scene a realistic single-clip duration — most around 5 seconds, a few up to ~8 when the motion genuinely needs it — and label it in the script (e.g. a "Scene 3 — 5s" heading). Reach the target length through the number of scenes, not by stretching clips or padding with repeated beats.

Style & genre (let this drive WHAT HAPPENS, not just the look):
- Style: Product Ad / ecommerce
- About: Fresh, tactile product content with lifestyle context and sensory detail. Designed for Instagram, DTC brands, e-commerce, and social-first campaigns.
- Genre cues: ecommerce, product, instagram, dtc, lifestyle, social

Style context (apply these aesthetics throughout):
- Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
- Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
- Lighting: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
- Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
- Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
- Camera work: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
- Reference works: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content

Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape — favor wide, cinematic compositions

response.content:
CORAL — A SUMMER LAUNCH

A launch film shot between shifts. Scarlett Doyle, 19, sells frozen pineapple at the Bondi kiosk and has 40 minutes before her break ends. She has one take, one shade, and a wave with bad timing. Voice: bright, wry, unbothered.

Scene 1 — 6s
INT. BONDI SHARE-HOUSE LAUNDRY — MORNING. A folding table jammed against a white tiled wall, ring light clipped to the dryer, a phone on a tripod. Scarlett — blonde, sun-freckled, kiosk polo half-tucked — drops into frame, slaps a cardboard mailer onto the table and rips the tape in one motion. Sunlight through the louvre window throws hard clean stripes across white cardboard and tissue paper. Handheld, slight micro-shake, eye-level. She looks up at the phone and says, "Okay — forty minutes. Go."

Scene 2 — 5s
MACRO, LOCKED. Fingers peel back cream tissue and lift a coral lipstick free of its bed — matte white tube, brushed gold band, condensation of morning light along the edge. Her thumb clicks the cap off and the coral bullet twists up, catching a bright specular flare. Shallow depth, warm highlights, crisp white ground.

Scene 3 — 5s
CLOSE, off-mirror angle over her shoulder. She swipes the coral once across her lower lip, presses her lips together, and immediately grins at her own reflection — no ceremony, cap already back on with a click. The tiled wall behind her glows white. Handheld drift in.

Scene 4 — 5s
OVERHEAD FLAT-LAY, locked, directly above. On a folded white towel: the coral tube, a set of kiosk keys, zinc-white sunscreen, a half-eaten frozen pineapple stick beading water, an elastic hair tie. Her hand enters, plucks the keys, and the towel shifts — the lipstick rolls a slow half-turn into the light and stops dead center.

Scene 5 — 6s
EXT. BONDI PROMENADE — LATE MORNING. Scarlett strides fast along the sea wall, phone held out at arm's length, hair lifting sideways in the wind, surfers cresting behind her in the mid-ground. She glances into the lens mid-stride and says, "Made for the water. Watch."

Scene 6 — 5s
EXT. KIOSK WINDOW. Direct on-camera flash, punchy editorial. Scarlett leans through the service hatch, coral mouth, hands sliding a paper cup of pineapple across the counter to a stranger's waiting fingers. Steam of cold — the cup sweats. She flicks her eyebrows at the lens. Locked frame, hard flash shadow on white paint.

Scene 7 — 5s
MACRO ON HER MOUTH AND JAW, three-quarter profile, sunlight raking. She drinks straight from a metal water bottle, a bead of water tracking down her chin; she wipes it away with the back of her wrist. The coral stays. Handheld, shallow focus.

Scene 8 — 6s
EXT. SHORELINE — AFTERNOON. She sets the phone-tripod in wet sand, backs up two steps into the frame, and starts her polished line — and a shorebreak wave surges in over her ankles, knocking the tripod sideways. The horizon tilts hard as the camera falls. Water rushes the lens. Handheld chaos, real light.

Scene 9 — 5s
LOW ANGLE, camera half-buried in wet sand at the waterline. The coral tube lies in the foam, gold band winking, as retreating water sluices around it and carves a bright channel in the sand. A tanned hand plunges in and snatches it up, dripping.

Scene 10 — 6s
EXT. SHORELINE, WIDER. Scarlett, soaked to the thigh, laughing so hard she doubles over, wet hair stuck to one cheek, tube held up in triumph. She straightens, pushes the hair back, and says to the lens, "Still on."

Scene 11 — 6s
FINAL FRAME. Late-afternoon glow, waist-up, salt drying white on her forearm. She rolls the coral bullet up, presses it once to her lips, clicks the cap shut and tosses the tube up — it flips once in the golden air and lands back in her palm as she turns toward the surf and walks in, ankle-deep, water flashing around her.
